title: Factorization through a relative curve
statement: Let $S$ be either the spectrum of a field or an excellent integral trait [def-exc-excellent-ring, def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], with generic point $s$, and let $X\to S$ be proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], dominant, finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], with $X$ integral [def-pc-integral-scheme]. If the generic fibre $X_s$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] has dimension $d\geq1$ [def-kun-dimension], then there are an excellent integral scheme $Y$ [def-exc-excellent-ring, def-pc-integral-scheme], a projective [def-kun-projective] dominant finite-type morphism $Y\to S$ whose generic fibre $Y_s$ has dimension $d-1$, an excellent integral scheme $X_0$, a proper dominant generically finite morphism $a:X_0\to X$ (finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] over a dense open of $X$), and a proper dominant morphism $g:X_0\to Y$ such that the composites $X_0\xrightarrow{a}X\to S$ and $X_0\xrightarrow{g}Y\to S$ are equal, and such that the extension of function fields $\kappa(Y)\subset\kappa(X_0)$ induced by $g$ has transcendence degree one [def-kun-transcendence-degree]. Here an integral trait is the spectrum of a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]; for any integral scheme $T$, $\kappa(T)$ means the residue field [def-weil-residue-field] at its generic point [def-sc-generic-point]. Excellence of a scheme means excellence of its affine coordinate rings.

source.place: Expose X, proof of Theorem 3.5, Step 5, printed p. 163: choose a rational map h' with relative transcendence degree one and take the schematic image after a projective modification.

proof.text: Write $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $k=\kappa(s)$ and $K=\kappa(X)$. Dominance sends the generic point of $X$ to $s$. The generic fibre is integral: on affine charts its rings are localizations of domains by $A\setminus\{0\}$, and its generic point is the generic point of $X$, with residue field $K$. It is of finite type over $k$, since localizing a finite list of algebra generators preserves that list. Thus [lem-sc-closed-irreducible-dimension-trdeg], applied to the entire generic fibre, gives $\operatorname{trdeg}_kK=d$. A nonempty affine chart in this fibre has a finite-type domain as coordinate ring and fraction field $K$ by [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction]; its algebra generators generate $K$ as a field. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finitely-generated-field-finite-transcendence-basis] and the definition of transcendence degree to choose a basis $t_1,\ldots,t_d$ of $K/k$.

source.place: Expose X, proof of Theorem 3.5, Step 5, printed p. 163; explicit rational-map/graph construction

proof.text: Set $n=d-1$ and $Y=\mathbf P^n_S$. Its standard charts are $\operatorname{Spec}A[z_1,\ldots,z_n]$ by [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-standard-charts]. They are domains, and their generic points coincide on their nonempty pairwise overlaps, so $Y$ is integral; each chart maps its generic point to $s$, so $Y\to S$ is dominant. The identity closed embedding into $\mathbf P^n_S$ proves projectivity by [def-kun-projective], and [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper] gives properness, hence finite type. The same chart description after replacing $A$ by $k$ gives $\kappa(Y_s)=k(z_1,\ldots,z_n)$; the indeterminates are a transcendence basis. Hence [lem-sc-closed-irreducible-dimension-trdeg] gives $\dim Y_s=n$. For $n=0$ the chart is $\operatorname{Spec}A$ and the field is $k$.

source.place: Expose X, proof of Theorem 3.5, Step 5, printed p. 163; explicit rational-map/graph construction

proof.text: Choose a nonempty affine $V=\operatorname{Spec}B\subset X$ from a finite-type affine cover over $A$. By [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction], write $t_i=b_i/c_i$ with $b_i,c_i\in B$ and $c_i\ne0$, for $1\le i\le n$. Put $c=\prod_i c_i$ (empty product $1$), and $U=\operatorname{Spec}B[1/c]$. This is nonempty and dense in $X$. The $A$-algebra map $A[z_1,\ldots,z_n]\to B[1/c]$, $z_i\mapsto t_i$, gives an $S$-morphism $r:U\to Y$ into the standard affine chart, by [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-standard-charts]. Its composite into $K$ is injective: $A\subset k$ and the $t_i$ are algebraically independent over $k$. Thus the generic point maps to the zero prime of this chart, the generic point of $Y$, so $r$ is dominant and induces $\kappa(Y)=k(t_1,\ldots,t_n)\subset K$.

source.place: Expose X, proof of Theorem 3.5, Step 5, printed p. 163; explicit rational-map/graph construction

proof.text: Let $\gamma=(j,r):U\to X\times_SY$, where $j:U\hookrightarrow X$. The ring $A$ is Noetherian (a field, or an excellent ring). Thus $U$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Every open of a Noetherian space is quasi-compact: otherwise a cover without a finite subcover gives a strictly increasing infinite chain of finite unions of its members. Consequently $j$ and $\gamma$ are quasi-compact, since preimages of affine opens are opens in $U$. Let $i:X_0\hookrightarrow X\times_SY$ be the scheme-theoretic image, with its factor map from $U$, supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-image-qc-kernel]. Write $a=\operatorname{pr}_X i$ and $g=\operatorname{pr}_Y i$. As $Y\to S$ is separated, [lemma-nagata-scheme-image-partial-section] says $a^{-1}(U)\to U$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Expose X, proof of Theorem 3.5, Step 5, printed p. 163; explicit rational-map/graph construction

proof.text: The support of $X_0$ is the closure of $\gamma(U)$ by [lemma-nagata-scheme-image-ideal-qc], so it is nonempty and irreducible. To check reducedness explicitly, take an affine open $W$ in $X\times_SY$ meeting $X_0$. The open $\gamma^{-1}(W)$ is nonempty by density. Its sections inject into $K$ by [lem-sc-integral-scheme-stalks-in-function-field], applied to the integral scheme $U$. The affine ideal defining $X_0\cap W$ is $\ker(\mathcal O(W)\to\mathcal O_U(\gamma^{-1}W))$ by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-image-qc-kernel]. This is a prime ideal, since the target embeds in a field; the quotient is therefore a domain. These affine charts cover $X_0$, so $X_0$ is reduced, hence integral. The open $a^{-1}(U)\cong U$ is dense in $X_0$.

source.place: Expose X, proof of Theorem 3.5, Step 5, printed p. 163; explicit rational-map/graph construction

proof.text: The projections $X\times_SY\to X$ and $X\times_SY\to Y$ are proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change], using respectively the properness of $Y\to S$ and the given properness of $X\to S$. Since $i$ is a closed immersion, [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper] makes both $a$ and $g$ proper. The image of $a$ contains the dense open $U$, and the image of $g$ contains the dense image $r(U)$, so both are dominant. The isomorphism $a^{-1}(U)\to U$ of [lemma-nagata-scheme-image-partial-section] is finite (on affine rings it is an isomorphism), so $a$ is generically finite in the required convention, with degree one.

source.place: Expose X, proof of Theorem 3.5, Step 5, printed p. 163; explicit rational-map/graph construction

proof.text: Identify $\kappa(X_0)$ with $K$ using the common nonempty affine open $a^{-1}(U)\cong U$ and [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction]. Under this identification, the field map induced by $g$ is the inclusion $k(t_1,\ldots,t_n)\subset K$ computed in step 3, since $g|_U=r$. The tower formula [lem-kun-transcendence-degree-tower] gives $d=n+\operatorname{trdeg}_{k(t_1,\ldots,t_n)}K$. The two known degrees are finite and $n=d-1$, so the remaining degree is one. This also treats $d=1$, when the intermediate field is simply $k$.

source.place: Expose X, proof of Theorem 3.5, Step 5, printed p. 163; explicit rational-map/graph construction

proof.text: The ring $A$ is excellent: this is assumed for a trait and follows from [lem-exc-fields-excellent] for a field. The scheme $Y$ is of finite type over $A$. The composite $X_0\xrightarrow aX\to S$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition], hence of finite type. For every affine open $W$ in either $Y$ or $X_0$, [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs] applied with the entire affine base $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ says $\mathcal O(W)$ is a finite-type $A$-algebra. It is excellent by [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent], taking the multiplicative subset $\{1\}$. This proves exactly the requested excellence of all affine coordinate rings.

source.place: Expose X, proof of Theorem 3.5, Step 5, printed p. 163; explicit rational-map/graph construction

proof.text: All maps were constructed over $S$: by the fibre-product relation, $(X\to S)\circ a=(Y\to S)\circ g$. With $X_0,Y,a,g$ as above, steps 2, 5, 6, 7 and 8 give every asserted clause. No finite-field, perfectness, separability or smoothness hypothesis was used.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q92-2064c93d6 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, all 22 proof deps and 12 stmt deps (by their statements), the parent lem-trf-alteration-relative-curve-preparation (step 1, its only citer), and the source ILO Travaux de Gabber X Thm 3.5 Step 5, printed p.163 (PDF pp.168-170). The statement is the source's rational-map construction followed by the schematic image in X x Y. It has the parent's hypotheses (S a field or an excellent trait; X proper, dominant, finite type, integral; d = dim X_s >= 1) and gives exactly the clauses the parent uses: dim Y_s = d-1, X_0 and Y excellent, relative trdeg 1. Nothing is weakened and no SGA source is cited. Step checks: (1) dominance makes A\{0} map to nonzero elements, so X_s is integral of finite type over k and the 0B1C node gives trdeg_k K = d. (2) Y = P^{d-1}_S is integral from its 01NG charts (nonempty overlaps), projective by def-kun-projective with the identity immersion, proper by the nagata node, and dim Y_s = d-1. (3) t_i = b_i/c_i; A[z] -> B[1/c] -> K is injective, so the generic point goes to the generic point of Y. (4) U is Noetherian, so j and gamma are quasi-compact; this is the hypothesis of the qc-kernel leaf and of the partial-section lemma, and Y/S is separated. (5) The image is irreducible as the closure of gamma(U), and each affine ideal is the kernel of a map into K, hence prime, so X_0 is integral. (6) Base change and closed-immersion (b) give a and g proper; both are dominant; a^{-1}U = U, so a is generically finite. (7) The trdeg tower gives relative degree 1, d=1 included. (8) 01T2 and 07QU give excellence. (9) The composites agree. Cases tested: d=1 (Y=S, X_0=X), X=P^d_S, the trait case P^1_A, and finite or imperfect k. There are no new nodes, and rg/blueprint search found no duplicate. Four tool_uses are needed and accepted: lem-sc-closed-irreducible-dimension-trdeg, lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-standard-charts, lem-exc-fields-excellent, lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent. The other declared entries are definitions, closed nodes or Mathlib leaves and need no tool_use. Minor: 'dominant' has no definition node anywhere in the DAG (the parent does the same). No fixes written.

lean.statement: theorem exists_relativeCurveFactorization {S X : Scheme.{u}} (hS : (∃ (k : Type u) (_ : Field k), Nonempty (S ≅ Spec (.of k))) ∨ ∃ (R : Type u) (_ : CommRing R) (_ : IsDomain R) (_ : IsDiscreteValuationRing R), IsExcellent R ∧ Nonempty (S ≅ Spec (.of R))) (s : S) (hs : IsGenericPoint s Set.univ) (f : X ⟶ S) [IsProper f] [IsDominant f] [IsIntegral X] (hft : LocallyOfFiniteType f ∧ QuasiCompact f) (d : ℕ) (hd : 1 ≤ d) (hdim : topologicalKrullDim (f.fiber s) = (d : WithBot ℕ∞)) : ∃ (Y : Scheme.{u}) (q : Y ⟶ S) (X₀ : Scheme.{u}) (a : X₀ ⟶ X) (g : X₀ ⟶ Y), (∀ U : Y.Opens, IsAffineOpen U → IsExcellent Γ(Y, U)) ∧ IsIntegral Y ∧ IsHProjective q ∧ IsDominant q ∧ LocallyOfFiniteType q ∧ QuasiCompact q ∧ topologicalKrullDim (q.fiber s) = ((d - 1 : ℕ) : WithBot ℕ∞) ∧ (∀ U : X₀.Opens, IsAffineOpen U → IsExcellent Γ(X₀, U)) ∧ IsIntegral X₀ ∧ IsProper a ∧ IsDominant a ∧ (∃ U : X.Opens, Dense (U : Set X) ∧ IsFinite (a ∣_ U)) ∧ IsProper g ∧ IsDominant g ∧ a ≫ f = g ≫ q ∧ ∃ η : X₀, IsGenericPoint η Set.univ ∧ @Algebra.trdeg (Y.residueField (g η)) (X₀.residueField η) _ _ (g.residueFieldMap η).hom.toAlgebra = 1
